comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological limitation (C109-C110). Both acknowledge bicuculline's non-specific effects beyond GABA blockade. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (appropriate acknowledgment), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting this limits mechanistic interpretation about GABAergic inhibition specifically.

Strong agreement on histological evidence (C34-C42). Both confirm specific activation patterns and lack of RTN/PHOX2B+ overlap. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative support, peer reviewer (R2) explicitly affirms histological confirmation of injection specificity. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on temporal dynamics (C51-C58). Both affirm rostro-caudal gradients in response duration, coupling strength, and onset latency. OpenEval provides detailed statistical support, peer reviewers confirm these findings as part of comprehensive characterization. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on novel analytical methods (C29-C30, C95-C106, C137-C147). Both praise 3D trajectory mapping and phase-plane analysis. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and ability to detect subtle differences; peer reviewers (R2, R3) explicitly commend innovative methods. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on methodological innovation (C137-C143). Both recognize novelty and utility of analytical approaches. OpenEval emphasizes robustness to variability; peer reviewers praise comprehensive functional mapping. Both rate as SUPPORTED, with overlap on claims about methodological contributions.

Strong agreement on phase-specific ABD analysis (C81-C94). Both affirm differentiation of rostral vs caudal responses across respiratory phases. OpenEval provides detailed statistical support; peer reviewers confirm convincing demonstration of ABD activation patterns. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on respiratory parameter changes (C63-C73). Both confirm rostral-caudal differences in VE, tidal volume, and timing parameters. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis; peer reviewers explicitly affirm robust changes in ventilation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on basic ABD response patterns (C6-C7, C25, C43-C50). Both affirm spatial gradient in response characteristics and EMG patterns. OpenEval details reliability and component characteristics; peer reviewers (all three) explicitly confirm solid evidence for pharmacological mapping findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on metabolic consequences (C74-C80). Both confirm selective VO2 decrease at rostral sites with increased VE demonstrating hyperventilation. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation remains speculative; peer reviewers affirm findings without questioning metabolic measurements. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Divergence on mechanistic interpretation (C148, C158-C160). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting inference about distinct neuronal populations is speculative without cellular characterization. Peer reviewer (R3) raises stronger concern that pharmacological approach cannot distinguish rhythmogenic from tonic neurons, fundamentally limiting mechanistic conclusions. Peer rates as UNCERTAIN with more critical stance.

Partial overlap on interpretive claims (C159-C160). OpenEval questions whether +0.6mm is 'most critical' and notes PHOX2B-negative conclusion has spatial limits. Peer reviewers don't directly address these specific interpretive nuances but affirm overall significance of findings.

Agreement on significance with different emphasis (C161-C162). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting future impact claims are speculative. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, emphasizing value for understanding neural control and as methodological framework, though acknowledging limitations. Both recognize contribution but differ on confidence level.

Overlap on future directions (C152). OpenEval rates suggestions for phenotypic characterization as SUPPORTED (appropriate future work). Peer reviewer (R3) implicitly supports this by noting limitation that cellular-level data is needed to understand whether effects involve rhythmogenic vs tonic neurons.

Agreement on PHOX2B findings (C157-C158). Both affirm histological data showing minimal PHOX2B activation rostral to +0.1mm. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewer explicitly confirms this anatomical finding. No disagreement on the data itself.

OpenEval evaluates background literature characterization (C3-C5, C16-C21) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers focus on experimental findings rather than literature review accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates citation accuracy and gap identification (C107-C108, C122-C125) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation - peer reviewers don't specifically assess literature review completeness.

OpenEval rates comparison to prior work (C128-C134) as UNCERTAIN, noting Bötzinger hypothesis is speculative and claim about absence of rostral studies may overstate gap. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific comparative claims.

OpenEval rates VO2 mechanism hypothesis (C136) as UNCERTAIN without direct work-of-breathing measurements. No corresponding peer review evaluation - peer reviewers don't specifically address this mechanistic speculation.
OpenEval evaluates established background knowledge (C1-C2, C10-C13, C22-C24, C111-C117, C149-C151) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation of background accuracy.
OpenEval evaluates basic methodological details (C31-C33) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation - peer reviewers don't specifically assess these standard methodological claims.

Peer reviewers affirm overall pharmacological mapping findings (C6-C8, C25-C28, C43-C46, C59-C60) with all three reviewers providing explicit support. OpenEval addresses these claims across multiple results (R2, R3, R4) but peer R1 groups them as unified finding about rostral location importance.

Peer reviewers specifically affirm ABD response characterization including claims C47-C50, C61-C62 that OpenEval distributes across R2 and R4. Peer review groups these as unified evidence for rostral location effects on ABD activation strength and duration.

Peer reviewers affirm temporal dynamics findings (C51-C58) that OpenEval evaluates in R3. Both reach same SUPPORTED conclusion but peer review doesn't separately evaluate the detailed statistical claims OpenEval emphasizes.
